newsitem.title: INDIA: India liberalises foreign equity approvals.
newsitem.headline: India liberalises foreign equity approvals.

text.p: The Indian cabinet on Tuesday decided to allow automatic approval for foreign equity of up to 51 percent in 16 more categories of industries, the Industry Ministry said.

It also decided for the first time to approve up to 74 percent foreign equity in nine industry groups linked to high-priority areas like infrastructure, non-conventional energy and electronic software, the ministry said in a statement.
The government has also decided to allow automatic approval for foreign equity up to 50 percent in some select mining industries, Industry Secretary N. Mohanty told a news conference in New Delhi.
Until now, the government allowed "automatic approval" of up to 51 percent foreign equity in 35 industries. The list will now have 51 industries.

"Only high priority industries have been included in the industry groups eligible for foreign equity up to 74 percent," said Mohanty, top-ranking civil servant in the Industry Ministry. "It is for the first time that this has been allowed."
The list of industry groups in which automatic approval of foreign equity up to 74 percent have been allowed are:

Mining services, basic metals and alloys, electrical generation and transmission, non-conventional energy generation and distribution, construction, land transport, water transport, storage and warehousing services and other manufacturing industries which include solar energy equipment, wind electric generators and navigational, metrological and geophysical instruments.
The list of industries in which automatic approval for foreign equity up to 51 percent would be granted are:

Food products, cotton textiles, wool, silk and man-made fibre textiles, water-proof textile fabrics, basic chemicals and chemical products (except products of petroleum and coal), rubber, plastics, petroleum and coal products, metal products and parts (except machinery and equipment), machinery and equipment other than transport equipment, land transport support services, water transport support services, services related to transport, renting and leasing and business services.

The Industry Ministry said in the statement that 1,401 proposals of foreign direct investment (FDI) worth 343.6 billion rupees were approved in the January-November period in 1996 compared to 1,335 proposals worth 320.71 billion rupees in the entire year in 1995.
The statement said actual inflow of foreign investment had grown in 1996.

"While during the entire year of 1995 the inflow of FDI was of the order of 63.7 billion rupees, this amount in the first 10 months (upto October) of 1996 have been of the order of 63.1 billion," it said. $1=35.8 rupees
